etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle French ingredient, from Latin ingrediens, present participle of ingredior (“I go or enter into or onto”).

definitions.definition: One of the substances present in a mixture, especially food.

quote.citation: 1704, I[saac] N[ewton], “(please specify |book=1 to 3)”, in Opticks: Or, A Treatise of the Reflexions, Refractions, Inflexions and Colours of Light. […], London:  […]  Sam[uel] Smith, and Benj[amin] Walford, printers to the Royal Society, […], →OCLC:
quote.text: By way of analysis we may proceed from compounds to ingredients.

quote.citation: 1731, John Arbuthnot, An Essay Concerning the Nature of Aliments, and the Choice of Them, According to the Different Constitutions of Human Bodies. […], London:  […]  J[acob] Tonson […], →OCLC:
quote.text: Water is the chief ingredient in all the animal fluids and solids.

definitions.definition: (figurative) Necessary element to achieve a certain goal, component.
